output.summary: The record FY2026 result is mainly a commodity price effect: revenue rose 46.5% on a 46% corn price rise while bushels fell 0.9%. Peers with no new program did as well. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes entirely from maintenance cut 905K to 612K, while the deferred backlog tripled to 1.26M. Harlan Junction has insurer-flagged dust and monitoring failures, and the SP-04 investigation of the leg #2 near-miss was never done. Staff report concerns, but nothing changes, so fear of reprisal is not the problem. Drying and grading depend on one retiring superintendent with no successor. The expansion case ignores price normalization and has no margin or debt-service projection. Fix safety hazards, start succession, rebuild the case, and defer the vote.
